description: Pip Tumbler comes up Sprocket Row on foot, to see how No. 9 is taking its bill. Pip is of no particular age and every particular opinion, and carries a receipt book in one pocket and a pencil for the spike in the other, and has not yet said which is wanted. Then Pip hangs a cap on the last tool hook above the bench, and the hook comes away from the wall. Something drops out of the gap behind it: a notebook's binding, marbled boards and a cloth spine, H. Vane inked inside the front in a small upright hand. Every page has been torn out at the stitching. "She was never without that," says Pip.

options.label: Make a pot of tea, and let Pip tell you about the street.

success.text: Pip takes three sugars and gives you Sprocket Row in return: who owes the pie shop, who owes the pawnbroker, and who on the street is no better than they ought to be, which is everybody. By the second cup you know more about Sprocket Row than Sprocket Row does. At the door Pip says, "Hester never made me tea," and then, "Well. Once," and goes.

options.label: Ask Pip when Pip last saw Hester Vane.

success.text: Pip thinks about it. "The Friday before she went. A toffee for me and the rent next week, same as ever. Wrote everything down, same as ever. Everything. What the Boiler said, what the tube said, what I said." Pip looks round the workshop. "You've moved the bench." You have not moved the bench. Pip looks at it a while longer anyway, then remembers another canister, somewhere else, and goes.
